title: IndoBias: A Dual Track Culturally Grounded Benchmark for LLMs Bias Evaluation in Indonesian Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring model perplexity on contrastive stereotypical vs. counter-stereotypical sentence pairs, and evaluating the stereotype polarity of generated responses across 7 tasks for 81 distinct Indonesian ethnic groups and cultural affiliations.
Evaluating stereotype polarity in generation tasks across 29 religious identities and measuring perplexity differences on contrastive sentence pairs related to religious affiliation and morality.
Assessing stereotype polarity in LLM outputs when prompted with 20 political parties, and measuring perplexity on contrastive sentence pairs targeting political affiliation and ideology.
Comparing model perplexity on contrastive sentence pairs that target social class, occupational prestige, educational attainment, and economic status.
Measuring model perplexity on contrastive sentence pairs focusing on regional origin, domicile, and urban-rural divides.
Comparing model perplexity on contrastive sentence pairs reflecting traditional gender expectations and familial roles.
Measuring perplexity on contrastive sentence pairs contrasting older and younger generational cohorts regarding values and work ethic.
Evaluating stereotype polarity in generation-based tasks across 60 government institutions and 68 universities to measure biases regarding competence, corruption, and elite status.
